name: Business websites
promise: A branded site that represents your business around the clock.
blurb: The core build. Three packages, each a one-time price agreed before I start.
intro: Most people looking for a business like yours will decide whether to call you before they ever speak to you. They will do it on a phone, in under a minute, from a search result. A business website exists to win that minute.
That means the essentials come first: what you do, where you are, what it costs, and how to get hold of you. Everything else is arranged around those four.
Every build is custom-coded rather than assembled from a template, which is why it loads fast on mobile data and why changing something later does not mean fighting a page builder.
includes: Home, services, about and contact pages
Contact and quote forms that reach your inbox
Google Maps, hours and click to call
On-page SEO built in, not sold back to you
Hosting, SSL and backups on your care plan
Built for phones first

faq.q: What do you need from me to start?
faq.a: Your logo if you have one, photos of your own work, and a rough idea of what you want each page to say. If you have none of that, content preparation covers me gathering it with you. It is a listed fee between $100 and $175, not a surprise.

faq.q: Who owns the site when it is done?
faq.a: You do, and you own the domain outright because you bought it in your own name. The care plan covers hosting and updates, not custody of your own business.

faq.q: Why is a care plan required?
faq.a: A site nobody hosts, backs up or patches is not a working site. The plan starts at $45 a month, covers hosting, SSL, backups and monitoring, and includes edits. There is a 3-month minimum and then you can cancel with 30 days' notice.

name: Menu and services pages
promise: Everything you offer, on one page a customer can actually read.
blurb: Food, nails, detailing, lawn care. Any business with a list.
intro: A printed menu photographed and uploaded as a PDF is the most common mistake a small business makes online. It is unreadable at arm's length on a phone, invisible to Google, and out of date the day a price changes.

A real menu or services page is text. It scales to the screen, it can be searched, and changing a price takes a minute instead of a reprint. It works exactly the same whether you are listing tacos, nail treatments, detailing packages or lawn services.
Past about 20 items the job changes shape: it needs categories, filtering and a layout that survives scrolling. That is where the complex price applies, and it is the only thing that moves it.
includes: Every item as real text, not an image of text
Prices you can change without a redesign
Categories and sections once the list is long
Photos per item where you have them
Readable at arm's length on a phone

faq.q: What if I do not sell food?
faq.a: Then it is a services page and it works identically. A lawn care company listing five services and a restaurant listing sixty items are the same page with different amounts in it, which is exactly what simple and complex measure.

faq.q: Can I update the prices myself?
faq.a: Small price changes are covered by the edit allowance on your care plan, so you message me and it is done. If you want to make the changes yourself, self-editable content is a $225 power feature and it is built for exactly this.

name: Catering and quote pages
promise: Turn a big job enquiry into a lead you can actually follow up.
blurb: Lead capture for the jobs that need a conversation first.
intro: The jobs worth the most are the ones that need a conversation first: a wedding, a fleet, a full-property contract. Those enquiries arrive as a phone call you miss, or a message with none of the detail you need to quote.
A catering or quote page asks the right questions up front. You open your inbox to a date, a headcount and a budget instead of the word "hi".
The complex version is the one where the page also sells: your packages laid out, what each includes, and pricing tiers underneath them.
includes: A form that asks what you need in order to quote
Your packages laid out with what each includes
Enquiries delivered straight to your inbox
Works for catering, events, contracts or fleet work

faq.q: How is this different from the contact form?
faq.a: The contact form asks for a name and a message. This one asks the questions that decide whether you can take the job and what to charge for it: the date, the headcount, the specifics. It is the difference between an enquiry and a lead.

name: Booking integration
promise: Let clients book straight from your site, at any hour, without phone tag.
blurb: Calendly, Square, Booksy or Vagaro, wired into the site properly.
intro: Every booking made by phone costs you a call, and every call you miss costs you the booking. Someone deciding at nine at night will book the business that lets them and leave a voicemail for the one that does not.

I connect the booking system to your site so the availability people see is the availability you actually have, and so the booking buttons sit where someone has just decided to act rather than three scrolls below it.
If you take deposits or payment at the time of booking, that is a further $150 on top of either option. It is the part that stops no-shows, and it is worth costing separately rather than burying.
includes: Your platform embedded so it looks like part of the site
Calendly, Square, Booksy, Vagaro or similar
Booking buttons placed where people are ready to act
Payment or deposit collection, if you want it
Tested end to end before launch

faq.q: Do I need an account already?
faq.a: No, but having one makes it a standard setup rather than a complex one, and that is one of the things the price measures. If you do not have one, I will set it up and configure your services with you.

faq.q: Which platform should I use?
faq.a: Tell me how you take bookings today and I will tell you plainly. Most single-service businesses are well served by Calendly's free tier; salons and multi-staff operations usually need something like Square or Vagaro.

name: Brand Asset Setup
promise: Your existing logo, prepared so it works properly on a website.
blurb: Already have a logo? I prepare it for the web. No redesign.
intro: Plenty of businesses already have a logo, but only as a screenshot, a small image or a Facebook profile picture. It looks fine there and soft or jagged on a website.
This is the tidy-up. I take the logo you have and prepare it to load quickly, sit properly on the page and show up as the little icon in a browser tab. The logo itself is not redesigned or restyled.
How far it can go depends on the artwork you send. A clean vector file gives the best result, a small image can only be prepared so far, and I will tell you which one you have before I start.
includes: Web-ready logo files, prepared for your site
SVG and PNG versions, where your source artwork permits
Favicon package for browser tabs and home screens
Your logo exactly as it is, with no redesign

pricing.note: For a logo you already have. If it needs rebuilding rather than preparing, the Brand Starter Kit is the next step.

turnaroundNote: Timing is agreed when you send the artwork. It depends mostly on the condition of the original file.

faq.q: What if I only have a low-quality image?
faq.a: I prepare what your artwork allows. A small or blurry image cannot be made sharp, and I will say so before I start. If the logo needs rebuilding, that is what the Brand Starter Kit is for.

faq.q: Do I need this to order a website?
faq.a: No. If your logo is already in a usable shape, I use it as it is. This is for when it is not.

faq.q: Will these files work for print, signs or embroidery?
faq.a: They are prepared for digital use. Digital files can be a starting point for print, signage, vinyl, decals or embroidery, but whether they suit physical production has to be confirmed with the vendor making the item, through their own proofing process.

name: Brand Starter Kit
promise: A straightforward, professional logo for a business that does not have one yet.
blurb: Need a straightforward new logo? Two concepts, delivered web-ready.
intro: For the business with a name and no mark. This is a clean, considered logo built from type and simple shapes: a wordmark, a monogram, a typography-based mark or a simple geometric or custom symbol.
You get two genuinely different concepts to choose between, not one idea in two colors. Pick a direction, send one round of revisions and I finish it and deliver the files.
It is designed to sit next to a website, so it has to read at small sizes, on light and dark backgrounds and as a favicon.
If what you have in mind is more elaborate, such as a detailed emblem or a fuller set of variants, that is Custom Identity.
includes: Two distinct logo concepts
One round of revisions on the concept you choose
Primary logo
SVG and PNG files
Light and dark variants
Icon or symbol version, where it applies
Favicon package

pricing.note: Two concepts and one revision round are included. A round is one consolidated list of changes.

turnaroundNote: Timing is agreed when we start. It depends on how quickly you choose a concept and send your revision notes.

faq.q: What kind of logos does this cover?
faq.a: Wordmarks, monograms, typography-based marks and simple geometric or custom symbols. Detailed mascots, hand-drawn illustration and specialized lettering are outside what I do in-house.

faq.q: What if I want more concepts or more revisions?
faq.a: An additional concept is $35 and an additional revision round is $50. Either is agreed with you before I start on it.

faq.q: Can you check that my name and logo are not already trademarked?
faq.a: No. I do not perform trademark searches or trademark clearance, and I cannot tell you a name or mark is free to use. Confirming that it does not infringe existing rights is your responsibility, and an attorney is the right person to ask.

faq.q: Can the files go straight to a printer, sign maker or embroiderer?
faq.a: The files are prepared for digital use and can be a starting point for physical production. I do not supply validated Pantone, CMYK, vinyl, thread or embroidery specifications, so final suitability is confirmed with the vendor through their own proofing process.

name: Custom Identity
promise: A more developed, custom identity for a business that needs more than a simple mark.
blurb: Need something more custom? Developed marks and expanded variants, quoted to fit.
intro: For the business whose identity has to do more work: a constructed mark rather than a simple wordmark, an emblem or badge, a logo that adapts cleanly across sizes and layouts.
It is scoped to the job. We talk through what you need, I quote it and you approve the figure before I start.
The work is done in-house and built for digital use: your website, social profiles, listings and the files that go with them.
includes: A custom-constructed mark, more developed than the Starter Kit
Emblems or badges, where they suit the business
Responsive logo variants, where appropriate
Expanded lockups and variants
Broader digital asset preparation
Concise usage guidance

pricing.heading: Priced to the project.
pricing.note: Custom Identity projects start at $550 and are quoted according to complexity and deliverables. You approve the figure before any work begins.

callout.title: When it needs a specialist
callout.body: Detailed mascots, character or hand-drawn illustration and specialized lettering are outside what I do in-house. I can coordinate an outside designer for $75, and you pay the designer or platform directly. If you only want a referral and would rather manage them yourself, there is no coordination charge.

turnaroundNote: Timing is set in the quote, because it depends on the scope of the work.

faq.q: Why is it a starting price rather than a fixed one?
faq.a: Identity work varies a lot. A single developed mark and a full set of lockups and variants are different amounts of work, so I quote it once I understand the scope, and you approve it before I start. $550 is where it starts, not a fixed price or a ceiling.

faq.q: What if I need a mascot or hand-drawn illustration?
faq.a: That is outside my in-house scope and may need an outside specialist. I can coordinate one for $75, which covers my project handling, while you pay the specialist or platform directly. If you would rather have a referral and manage them yourself, the $75 does not apply. Third-party costs are yours unless we agree otherwise in writing.

faq.q: Is this a full brand guidelines package?
faq.a: No. It includes concise usage guidance covering how to use the logo and its variants, not a full brand manual.

faq.q: Do you check that my name and logo are clear to use?
faq.a: No. I do not perform trademark searches or trademark clearance. Confirming that a name or mark does not infringe existing rights is your responsibility.

faq.q: Will the files be ready for signage, vinyl, decals or embroidery?
faq.a: They can be prepared as digital files for those uses, but I do not supply validated production specifications. Final suitability is confirmed through the relevant vendor and their proofing process.

blurb: Google Business Profile and Facebook covers, plus one square graphic.
intro: When someone looks you up, the first thing they see is often a cover image rather than your site. A blank or mismatched one makes a business look unfinished.

This set gives your Google Business Profile and Facebook page a matching cover, plus one square graphic you can reuse for posts. It is built around your existing logo and colors, so every profile reads as the same business.

faq.q: Do I need a logo before ordering?
faq.a: Yes, a usable one. If you have a logo that needs preparing, that is Brand Asset Setup. If you do not have one, that is the Brand Starter Kit.

faq.q: Can I get other sizes or platforms?
faq.a: The set is the three pieces listed. Anything beyond them is a separate conversation, and I will tell you the price before I start.

name: Care plans
promise: The site stays hosted, secure, backed up and current, without you touching it.
blurb: Required with every build. $45 or $95 a month.
intro: Hours change. Prices change. You get better photos. A site still showing last year's information does more damage than no site at all, because it teaches people your business cannot be trusted on detail.

A care plan is what keeps that from happening, and it is required with every build. That is not an upsell: a site nobody hosts, patches or backs up is not a working site, and I am not willing to hand over something that will quietly break six months later.
Host keeps the site online and current. Grow adds real monthly work on top: four updates, faster turnaround, and your Google Business Profile managed rather than just created.
includes: Hosting, SSL and daily backups
Uptime monitoring
Edits handled by me, with no CMS to learn
Google Business Profile management on Grow
A monthly performance report on Grow
3-month minimum, then 30 days' notice

faq.q: What counts as one update?
faq.a: One request, however many small changes are in it. Sending four photos to swap is one update, not four. Host covers up to 15 minutes of edits a month; Grow covers four updates a month with a 3-business-day turnaround.

faq.q: How do I request a change?
faq.a: You message me. You work directly with ALVSolutions — no ticket queue or outsourced support.

faq.q: What if I need more than my plan covers?
faq.a: Anything beyond the allowance is priced by size and published: $30 minor, $60 moderate, $100 substantial. You will get told which bracket a job lands in before I do it.

faq.q: Can I cancel?
faq.a: After the 3-month minimum, with 30 days' notice. Cancellation takes effect at the end of your current billing period, and that period is not refunded. After that I stop hosting, maintaining and monitoring the site. The site is yours either way: nothing is deleted, and I will help you move it to hosting you control, though any third-party cost to do that is yours.

name: Google Business Profile
promise: The listing that shows up in the map pack, set up in your own account.
blurb: $200 standalone. Setup assistance in Standard and Complete, managed on Grow.
intro: For a local business, the Google Business Profile is often doing more work than the website is. It is the box with your hours, your photos, your reviews and a call button, and it appears above the search results rather than in them.

I set it up inside your own Google account, so it belongs to you and nobody has to ask my permission to change it later. Categories, service areas, hours, description, photos and the first review request all get handled.
Google controls verification timelines and anyone who promises you a date on that is guessing. What I can control is that everything is correct and complete the moment it goes live.
includes: Created or claimed in your own Google account
Categories and service areas chosen deliberately
Hours, description and contact details completed
Photos uploaded and named properly
Verification submitted and followed through
Posts and review responses handled on the Grow plan

pricing.note: Setup assistance is included in Standard and Complete. Ongoing management, posts and review responses are part of the Grow care plan at $95 a month.

faq.q: Whose account is it in?
faq.a: Yours. I work inside your Google account rather than creating one I control. If we part ways, the listing does not move.

faq.q: How long does verification take?
faq.a: Google decides that, and it ranges from a day to a few weeks depending on how they choose to verify you. I submit it and follow it through, but nobody can promise you a date.

faq.q: Is this SEO?
faq.a: It is the local half of it, and for a business with a service area it is usually the half that brings the phone calls. On-page SEO for the site itself is built into every package at no extra cost.

name: Business cards

Designing the card against the same brand as the site means the person who found you online and the person handed your card meet the same business.

Basic is design only: you get files prepared for professional printing to take to the printer you choose, who confirms final specifications and proofs. Premium is front and back on thick stock with a QR code, printed and delivered to you.
